name: STAM
main_result: DeiT-S (distilled): ImageNet top-1 76.35 with 20.5K pixels sensed (19 glimpses of 32x32; PatchDrop 76.00 with 27.9K)
notes: Reinforcement learning (one-step actor-critic). The agent never sees the full image: it senses one 32x32 glimpse (4 patches of 16x16) per step at a location chosen by an actor MLP from past glimpses, and only the patches of the sensed glimpses enter DeiT, so the token count is 4 x the number of glimpses. Default T=21 steps; an optional early-termination rule stops when the max class probability exceeds gamma (66.47% at 7.5 glimpses on average for gamma=0.5). Core initialized from pre-trained DeiT-distilled and trained 200 epochs on ImageNet with a consistency loss to a full-image teacher. Cost is given as pixels sensed, not FLOPs; no throughput. Active-vision (glimpse) method rather than token reduction inside a ViT.
evidence: "STAM sequentially observes informative glimpses (gt ) from an image. While never observing an image entirely, STAM predicts the class-label of an image (y) based on glimpses" (Fig. 1); "we adopt one-step actor-critic algorithm [41] to update the parameters at each time step" (4.2); "We initialize the core and the classifiers using a pretrained DeiTD" (5. Implementation); "Our agent runs for T = 21 time-steps per image, capturing one glimpse at a time" (5. Optimization)

name: AdaGlimpse
main_result: ViT-B encoder: ImageNet top-1 77.54 with 14 glimpses of 32x32 (28.57% of pixels; STAM 76.13); 76.30 with about 8.3 glimpses (16.94%) with early stopping
notes: Reinforcement learning (Soft Actor-Critic). The agent picks position and scale (x, y, z) of each glimpse in a continuous space; each glimpse is captured at a fixed d_cam x d_cam resolution and split into 16x16 patches, so the number of processed tokens is the number of glimpses so far times the patches per glimpse. Exploration stops at a maximum number of glimpses or when a confidence level is reached. The ViT-B encoder is pre-trained by the authors for 600 epochs with 196 random glimpses and then trained 100 epochs alternating backbone and agent; no external checkpoint is mentioned, so training is taken as from scratch. Teacher for distillation is a pre-trained DeiT III ViT. Also reconstruction (other) and ADE20K segmentation. No FLOPs or latency. Active visual exploration rather than token reduction inside a ViT.
evidence: "It uses Soft Actor-Critic, a reinforcement learning algorithm tailored for exploration tasks, to select glimpses of arbitrary position and scale" (Abstract); "The exploration process is stopped when a set confidence level or a maximum number of glimpses is reached" (3.1); "Additionally, we pre-train the model for 600 epochs with 196 random glimpses per image with sizes and positions sampled from a uniform distribution" (4. Training)

name: UCB bandit attention
backbones: ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-B/32; ViT-L/16; ViT-L/32; ViT-H/14; PiT-S; PiT-B; DINO ViT-S/8, ViT-B/8, ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16; EsViT-S, EsViT-B
main_result: ViT-S/16: top-1 81.7 at 4.1 GFLOPs, 2645 img/s (DeiT III ViT-S 81.4 at 4.6, 1891 img/s)
notes: Reinforcement learning (multi-armed bandit, UCB; no learned policy). In every attention block each query aggregates values only from the top-p (p=5) key positions ranked by attention score plus a UCB bonus that favours rarely selected positions; the sequence length is not reduced, so the method is closer to sparse attention than to token reduction. Trained from scratch with the DeiT recipe (UCB module switched on after 500 steps); the ViT-S row is a ViT-S/16 (DeiT-S size) trained this way, not a pruned pre-trained DeiT-S. Throughput on one V100 32GB, batch 256. Also audio classification. Code URL from the PDF hyperlink (the text shows 'bandit wacv').
evidence: "In this paradigm, each token is assigned a score that combines its attention score with the frequency of its selection. The top-p tokens with the highest combined scores are then chosen for further processing" (1. Introduction); "We select p > 0 positions with the highest µk,t as the hard attention tokens" (3.2); "During training the ViT as well as the UCB-based approach models, we have followed the training techniques used in DeiT [50]" (4. Experiments)

main_result: ViT-B/16 (MAE): ImageNet top-1 80.8 at about 10 GFLOPs (about 0.5 above ToMe and ToFu at the same budget, SNR 20 dB)
notes: Not RL: the per-layer cosine-similarity thresholds tau_l in [0.5, 1] are searched offline by multi-objective Bayesian optimization (Gaussian process + EHVI) on 500 ImageNet images, giving Pareto policies over accuracy, GFLOPs and number of transmitted tokens. ToMe-style alternating source/destination split; a source token merges into its most similar destination only if the similarity is at least tau_l (norm-weighted average), so the token count varies per image. The merged tokens are sent over a noisy channel with a SwinJSCC encoder (semantic communication). VQA at 55 GFLOPs: ScienceQA 69.9, GQA 61.8 (LLaVA 70.4 / 62.0 at about 191 GFLOPs). Read arXiv v1 (submitted version), not the published OJ-COMS text. Code 'will be made available' per the paper.
evidence: "This paper introduces a training-free framework for adaptive token merging, a novel mechanism that compresses transformer representations at runtime by selectively merging semantically redundant tokens under per-layer similarity thresholds" (Abstract); "We cast the discovery of merging strategies as a multi-objective optimization problem and leverage Bayesian optimization to obtain Pareto-optimal trade-offs" (Abstract); "This condition makes the number of merged tokens inherently data-dependent" (V. Methodology)

name: MaMe
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE ViT-B; MAE ViT-L; MAE ViT-H; AugReg ViT-B/16; ViT-T; ViT-S; ViT-B; Swin-T; Swin-S; Iwin-T; Iwin-S; CLIP ViT-L/14; SigLIP ViT-B/16; SigLIP2 ViT-B/16; LLaVA-1.5-7B; VideoMAE-B; VideoMAE-L
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 78.61 at 2.3 GFLOPs, 9015 img/s (training-free; baseline 79.82 at 4.6, 5039 img/s)
notes: Matrix-only merging: alternating destination/source split, cosine similarity shifted by a threshold tau with ReLU, column-normalized fusion weights with a per-source adaptive threshold; source tokens with no similar destination are kept ('preserved source tokens'), so the output length M + r depends on the input (made consistent within a batch). Training-free on DeiT/MAE (first 8 layers, tau=0.8, other settings as DiffRate) and from scratch (merging at layers 3, 6, 9 with 2:1 reduction; ViT-S 77.0 at 2.1 GFLOPs vs 79.8). Also used as downsampling in Swin/Iwin. DeiT-S throughput on A100, batch 1024, FP16; batch-1 throughput for CLIP/SigLIP on a 3090. Code URL from the arXiv extended version (MaMe & MaRe), not from the CVF paper. Not RL.
evidence: "We introduce MaMe, a training-free, differentiable token merging method that relies entirely on matrix operations to accelerate vision transformers" (Abstract); "To isolate the most significant relationships, we apply a rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation with a shifting threshold τ" (3.2); "A key component of our methodology is the preservation of unique source tokens" (3.3); "utilizing their pretrained weights without any fine-tuning. For these off-the-shelf experiments, we apply MaMe to the first 8 layers" (4.0.1)

name: AdaPerceiver
main_result: AdaPerceiver: ImageNet-1K top-1 85.4 at 100.8 GFLOPs (256 latent tokens); RL token policy 85.0 at 46.9 GFLOPs
notes: Perceiver-style model: input tokens are read by cross-attention into a chosen number of latent tokens (32-256), latent blocks use block-masked attention, Matryoshka FFNs (width) and early exits (depth). The token count is set at inference; reinforcement learning (REINFORCE) trains a lightweight policy that picks the token count per input, and an early-exit policy uses a confidence threshold. Pre-trained 150 epochs on ImageNet-12K with logit distillation from ViT-H, then only the readout and head are fine-tuned on ImageNet-1K. Throughput and latency on an A100 at batch 512. ADE20K: 43.9 mIoU at 158 encoder GFLOPs (ViT-H/14 44.2 at 4313). Adaptive architecture rather than token reduction inside a ViT.
evidence: "Cross-attention layers map input tokens to latent tokens and decode the latents to output tokens" (3.2.1); "token adaptivity by varying the number of latent tokens" (3.2.1); "RL Policy: We train a lightweight policy network using REINFORCE [45] to select a token count for an input" (4.5); "We pre-train our model on ImageNet-12K [44] for 150 epochs" (4.1)

name: SPOT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.7 at 3.0 GFLOPs (rho=0.7; baseline 79.8 at 4.6); 79.5 at 2.8
notes: A per-stage MLP predictor takes token embeddings plus compact attention statistics (class-token row and column, row/column mean and variance of the attention map) of the current and all preceding layers; Gumbel-Softmax masks drop tokens hierarchically at layers 4, 7, 10 with retention rate rho^k. Backbone and predictors are fine-tuned 80 epochs from pre-trained weights. Throughput appears only in the arXiv appendix (one SPOT variant 3,880 img/s at 3.0 GFLOPs and 79.5%, RTX 4090, batch 512), not for the 79.7 setting. Also plugged into SPViT and dTPS. Not RL.
evidence: "SPOT employs computationally lightweight predictors that can be plugged into various ViT architectures and learn to derive effective input-specific token prioritization across layers" (Abstract); "This process is characterized by a retention rate, ρ, which governs the proportion of tokens considered more informative and retained at each detection iteration" (3.2); "both the prediction modules and the transformer model underwent joint optimization and fine-tuning with a retention rate of ρ = 0.7" (4.1)

name: Dyna-ViT
main_result: ViT-B/16: ImageNet-1k top-1 82.3 at 13.40 GFLOPs, 313 img/s (K=70%; baseline 81.8 at 19.90, 210 img/s; supplementary)
notes: Before the encoder each 16x16 patch is scored by a parameter-free proxy (default L2 norm of the raw patch; Sobel and entropy in ablations) and only the top-K% patches (K=70) plus [CLS] are embedded into an unmodified ViT. The paper calls the method training-free, but all reported models are fine-tuned 5-10 epochs with the pruning in place from the ImageNet-21k checkpoint (ImageNet-1k: 10 epochs); top-K indices are precomputed per split. Main experiments on PASCAL VOC (5 classes), CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet; ImageNet-1k only in the supplement. Throughput on one T4 with AMP (batch not stated). The VOC DynamicViT baseline (46.0%) looks like a failed run. No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "Patches are ranked (e.g., by L2 energy) and only the top-K are kept; the backbone remains an unmodified ViT with standard [CLS] and positional embeddings" (Abstract); "Given a keep ratio K ∈ (0, 100], select" (3.2); "pretrained on ImageNet-21k and fine-tuned for each dataset" (Supplementary 3); "Training schedule: Batch size 128, 10 epochs, AdamW optimizer" (Supplementary 4, ImageNet Setup)

name: LeMeViT
main_result: LeMeViT-Small: ImageNet-1K top-1 81.88 at 3.74 GMACs, 3608 img/s (Swin-T 81.30 at 4.35, 2872 img/s)
notes: Hierarchical ViT with 16 learnable meta tokens initialized from image tokens by cross-attention; in the first two stages Dual Cross-Attention replaces self-attention (image tokens attend to meta tokens and meta tokens attend to image tokens), cutting the attention cost from O(N^2) to O(2MN). The number of image tokens is not reduced; the meta tokens act as a compact proxy. Trained 300 epochs from scratch on ImageNet-1K (DeiT settings); remote sensing models pre-trained on MillionAID and fine-tuned for DOTA detection, Potsdam segmentation and CDD change detection. Throughput with the timm benchmark on one RTX 4090 (batch not stated). Architecture design rather than token reduction.
evidence: "this paper proposes to use learnable meta tokens to formulate sparse tokens, which effectively learn key information meanwhile improving the inference speed" (Abstract); "the meta tokens are first initialized from image tokens via cross-attention" (Abstract); "The models are implemented by PyTorch and trained 300 epochs from scratch" (4.1)

name: ViTTM
main_result: ViTTM-B(28,28): ImageNet-1K top-1 82.9 at 7.08 GFLOPs, 234.1 ms (ViT-B/16 81.0 at 16.87, 529.5 ms; A100, batch 256)
notes: Two token streams: a few process tokens made with a larger patch size (e.g. 28 or 32 tokens) go through the encoder blocks, while many memory tokens (patch 16) are only read and written by linear-attention heads with add fusion in each block. Pre-trained on ImageNet-21K and fine-tuned on ImageNet-1K. ADE20K (Segmenter): 45.17 mIoU at 26.8 FPS on an A30 (ViT-B/16 45.65 at 13.8 FPS). Memory-augmented two-stream architecture rather than pruning or merging.
evidence: "By ensuring that there are fewer process tokens, we are able to reduce the inference time of the network while maintaining its accuracy" (Abstract); "This is achieved by using a larger patch size for process tokens" (3.2.1); "we pre-train our models on ImageNet-21K [30], and subsequently fine-tune them on ImageNet-1K [6] at 224px image resolution" (4.1)

name: RanMerFormer
notes: Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available; ScienceDirect blocked automated download and no preprint was found. Brain tumor MRI classification: a pre-trained ViT backbone with a token merging mechanism that removes redundant tokens, and a randomized vector functional-link (RVFL) head that trains quickly. How tokens are paired, how many are merged, whether the backbone is fine-tuned, the backbone names and all numbers could not be checked. Medical application paper.
evidence: "A pre-trained vision transformer is used as the backbone model. Then, a merging mechanism is proposed to remove the redundant tokens in the vision transformer, which improves computing efficiency substantially" (Abstract); "Finally, a randomized vector functional-link serves as the head in the proposed RanMerFormer, which can be trained swiftly" (Abstract)

name: TRAM
main_result: ViT-B (ImageNet pre-trained, 5-epoch fine-tuning): Imagenette 96.36 at 11.85 GFLOPs, 483 FPS (phi=75%; vanilla 97.43 at 16.88, 358 FPS)
notes: The attention maps of each layer (max over heads) form a multilayer network; a Token Relevance Centrality accumulates the attention a token receives from influential tokens over the current and previous layers (weighted by layer index), and the top phi_q tokens are kept (reduction every three layers, phi = 75% or 50%). The class token is not used, so it also works with SimpleViT; cls-attention is the closest value (attention statistics). Experiments train from scratch on CIFAR10, FMNIST and Imagenette (160x160, 10-50 epochs) and fine-tune ImageNet pre-trained ViT-B/ViT-S for 5 epochs; the abstract says it works without fine-tuning, but no such result was found. FPS on an RTX A2000 (batch not stated). No ImageNet-1k or DeiT-S numbers. Not RL.
evidence: "a new approach to evaluate the relevance of tokens based on a new centrality measure computed on the multilayer network" (Abstract); "TRAM may be considered a static pruning approach, in that it consistently maintains a predetermined number of tokens throughout the process" (2. Related work); "We then fine-tuned all models on CIFAR10, Imagenette and FMNIST for five epochs" (4.3)

name: IdleViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.1 GMACs, 3361.3 img/s (k=0.7; baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 2476.8 img/s)
notes: In each layer the top-K image tokens by [CLS] attention go through MHSA and FFN; the other tokens stay idle and are copied to the layer output, so they can be selected again in later layers (keep ratios 1, k, k^2, k^3 over four stages). 'halt' is the closest value: idle tokens skip a layer but are not stopped for good. A token cut loss (normalized graph cut on the attention map) is used only during fine-tuning. Fine-tuned 30 epochs from pre-trained weights with logit and feature distillation. Speed on one V100, batch 128. Not RL.
evidence: "in each layer, IdleViT selects a subset of the image tokens to participate in computations while keeping the rest of the tokens idle and directly passing them to this layer’s output" (Abstract); "image tokens with top-K attention scores towards the [CLS] token are selected and straightforwardly named the Selected tokens" (3.2); "All the models are finetuned for only 30 epochs" (4.1)

name: ATMformer
main_result: ATMformer: NWPU-RESISC45 (10% training) OA 94.7 at 636 img/s (Swin-B 92.0 at 589 img/s)
notes: Hierarchical ViT for remote sensing scene classification. Tokens are grouped by a space-filling-curve clustering for local attention; at each stage merging centers are picked by top-k over a grid prior plus a learned MLP importance score (k = N*r), and neighbours are aggregated into the centers with learned pairwise weights and a position-aware PointConv-style sum (3136 tokens down to 49). The paper calls it adaptive token merging; 'cluster' is used because neighbours are pooled into selected centers. Initialized from ImageNet-1K pre-trained weights and trained 120 epochs. No FLOPs; the GPU for throughput is not stated (training on RTX 4090). No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "we propose an adaptive token merging transformer (ATMformer) that preserves essential local features by estimating the importance score of each token" (Abstract); "where k = ⌊ N · r ⌋ is the target number of tokens to retain, and r is the sampling rate" (2.3.1); "We initialize our model with weights pretrained on the ImageNet-1K dataset" (3.2)

name: MSHViT (Sinkhorn tokenizer)
notes: Only the abstract was available (ScienceDirect and the Aalborg University repository blocked automated download). A CNN backbone is extended with a lightweight ViT that aggregates multi-scale features non-locally; a Sinkhorn clustering-based tokenizer with distinct cluster centers produces a smaller set of tokens. Evaluated on Sewer-ML multi-label sewer defect classification (up to +2.53 points). Token count, training, backbones and costs could not be checked. Application paper in which token reduction is part of the tokenizer.
evidence: "This paper describes the multi-scale hybrid vision transformer (MSHViT), an extension of the classical convolutional neural network (CNN) backbone, for multi-label sewer defect classification" (Abstract); "a smaller set of tokens was produced through a novel Sinkhorn clustering-based tokenizer using distinct cluster centers" (Abstract)

main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 76.55 at 2.98 GMACs, FPGA latency 1.953 ms (rb=0.7, rt=0.9, b=16; baseline 79.59 at 4.27 GMACs, 3.19 ms)
notes: Hardware co-design on a Xilinx Alveo U250 FPGA (int16, 300 MHz). Combines static block weight pruning (top-k rate rb) with EViT-style token dropping at layers 3, 7 and 10: head-averaged attention scores keep ceil((N-1) rt) tokens and the rest are fused into one token by score-weighted averaging. Simultaneous fine-pruning from pre-trained DeiT-S for 30 epochs with ViT-B distillation. Headline: average latency reduction of 12.8x vs CPU (EPYC 9654), 3.2x vs GPU (RTX 6000 Ada) and 0.7-2.1x vs prior FPGA accelerators; FPGA latency from hardware emulation at batch 1, throughput = 1/latency. Cost column is MACs (the paper reports 4.27G MACs for DeiT-S), and the accuracy also reflects weight pruning. No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "Based on a keep-rate rt , a total of ⌈(N − 1)rt ⌉ tokens with the top scores in S are retained" (IV-B); "The remaining inattentive tokens are fused into a single token by performing a weighted aggregation of these tokens with respect to their respective scores in S" (IV-B); "we use the pre-trained DeiT-Small model available at [47] with the classification MLP head parameters re-initialized" (VII-A); "All model variants are trained for a total of 30 epochs" (VII-A)

name: DRViT
notes: No text available: the article is paywalled, Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar have no abstract, and no preprint was found. The title describes a dynamic redundancy-aware ViT accelerator on FPGA built by algorithm-architecture co-design; the hardware platform is an FPGA per the title, and no speed-up or energy number could be checked. All method values are '?'.
evidence: "DRViT: A dynamic redundancy-aware vision transformer accelerator via algorithm and architecture co-design on FPGA" (Title)

name: ViT-ToGo
main_result: ViT-B: ImageNet top-1 79.60 at 12.86 GFLOPs (20% pruning at layers 4, 6, 8; baseline 80.05 at 17.58)
notes: Hardware co-design on a Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA (ViT-Tiny, 16-bit fixed point, 100 MHz). The Grouped Token Selector sums [CLS] attention over groups of adjacent patches, divides by a head importance (softmax of each head's [CLS] self-attention), sorts groups with a merge sort that runs in parallel with the FFN, and drops the lowest groups (20-30% at 3-4 layers). Headline hardware result: cycle count reduced to 70% of the baseline accelerator with 1.13% extra resources on average (power 4.057 W vs 3.937 W). Training for the CIFAR/ImageNet runs follows the ViT-pytorch repository without further detail; for the DeiT-S comparison the pre-trained model is fine-tuned one epoch. The DeiT-S table (Evo-ViT + grouped tokens) has a broken layout, so the DeiT-S columns are '?'. No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "To form groups, we sum the attention probabilities of spatially adjacent tokens within the image" (III-A); "Then, we rank these groups based on their calculated importance and retain only the tokens in the most significant groups" (III-A); "we used pretrained weight of DeiT-Small, and finetune with each method for one epoch" (V-B)

name: AdapTiV
notes: Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available. Hardware-software co-designed accelerator: Local Matching limits the merge search space, Sign Similarity simplifies token similarity, and a Dynamic Merge Rate makes the merging image-adaptive (whether by a threshold or another rule could not be checked, so schedule is '?'); merging latency is hidden inside LayerNorm by an Adaptive Token Merging Engine. Headline: average speed-ups of 309.4x, 18.4x, 89.8x and 6.3x and energy-efficiency gains of 262.1x, 21.5x, 496.6x and 11.2x over edge CPUs, edge GPUs, server CPUs and server GPUs, with accuracy loss below 1% and no extra training. Hardware platform details, task and backbones could not be checked. Not RL.
evidence: "AdapTiV incorporates algorithmic innovations such as Local Matching, which restricts the search space for token merging, thereby reducing the computational complexity; Sign Similarity, which simplifies the calculation of similarity between tokens; and Dynamic Merge Rate, which enables image-adaptive token merging" (Abstract); "while maintaining an accuracy loss below 1 % without additional training" (Abstract)
